summary.oneLiner: Gillette India Limited is the Indian arm of Procter & Gamble that manufactures and sells branded packaged fast-moving consumer goods in the grooming and oral care categories, anchored on the Gillette and Oral-B brands.
summary.business: The Company, incorporated in India in 1984 as Indian Shaving Products Limited and acquired by P&G in 2005, is engaged in manufacturing and selling branded packaged fast moving consumer goods in the grooming and oral care businesses. currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no named plant, capacity or capex project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Expansion in this Annual Report is described in market-reach rather than asset terms: the Company continued to expand the reach of Gillette Guard through focused communication and strong market execution, launched Gillette Guard 3-in-1, strengthened the Mach3 range, and in Oral Care pursued a strategic focus on expanding penetration of electric toothbrushes, launched kids' battery toothbrushes and its biggest-ever launch in the sensitive toothbrush category, working to make the Sensitive Care range widely available across channels and segments through e-commerce and general trade activations. On investment intensity, the BRSR states that because the Company avails the benefit of the Procter & Gamble group's research and development across the globe, it incurred no expenditure on research and development during the Financial Year, and that it spends from time to time on energy efficient equipment such as energy efficient pumps and lighting, with spend on such equipment not substantial versus the Company's total capital expenditure during the year.

risks.risk: Workplace safety at manufacturing sites deteriorated versus the prior period
risks.note: BRSR safety incident data shows worker Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate of 2.60 per one million person-hours in 2025-26 against Nil in 2024-25, two total recordable work-related worker injuries against Nil, and one high-consequence work-related injury or ill-health (excluding fatalities) against Nil; no fatalities were reported. The Company states it maintains an occupational health and safety management system covering all employees, workers and external parties who work at or visit its sites.

risks.risk: Consumer demand environment - shifting FMCG consumption and inflation-linked softness
risks.note: Management notes the FMCG sector is expected to enter a stabilization phase with growth projected to be volume-led rather than price-driven, with urban demand anchoring growth aided by premiumisation. Growth therefore depends on volume and mix rather than pricing, and management describes its outlook as only cautiously optimistic.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance exposure across a wide body of applicable laws
risks.note: The Company states it operates within the letter and spirit of all applicable laws, has set in place mechanisms for meeting compliance requirements with periodic monitoring to avoid deviations and regular updates to keep pace with regulatory changes, and runs recurring employee training on Global Anti-Corruption Standards, Prevention of Sexual Harassment, whistle-blower mechanism, conflict of interest, data privacy, data integrity and anti-trust compliance.

risks.risk: Dependence on third-party distributors and vendors
risks.note: The Board's report states the Company has a very stringent system for assessment of distributors and vendors before selection, indicating that channel and supplier counterparties are a monitored exposure in the risk framework.

risks.risk: Protection of assets, personnel and confidential/personal data
risks.note: The internal controls section describes systems designed to protect the Company's assets and confidential information, including personally identifiable information, against financial losses and unauthorized use; the security section describes comprehensive security programmes at offices and plants with a regular security risk assessment, and reports no major security breaches or incidents at the plant during the Financial Year.

risks.risk: Residual enterprise risk - not all risks can be eliminated
risks.note: The Company has a Risk Management Committee and a risk management policy, identifies risks by a consistent process across functions and links each risk to a mitigation step, with the risk report reviewed at regular intervals; management explicitly acknowledges that not all risks can be eliminated and relies on insurance coverage to protect the value of its assets.

risks.risk: Internal control and SOX-compliance execution across key business processes
risks.note: Controls Self-Assessments, a continuous monitoring toolkit for manufacturing processes (packing, planning, warehousing) with auto-sampled quarterly testing, and assessments of high-risk and SOX compliance areas by P&G's Global Internal Audit team are the stated defences; issues raised are tagged to business owners for remediation and reported to senior leadership, and a Governance Board led by the Managing Director reviews enterprise level risks.

one-line thesis: Gillette India delivered FY26 sales of ~₹3,100cr (+8%) and PAT of ~₹650cr (+23%), extending a 5-year run of consistent double-digit sales and ~17% CAGR profit growth with ~600bps net-margin expansion. Headline topline growth looks muted because a one-time base — the closure of the Bangladesh affiliate distribution agreement — depressed export revenue; management says ex-that, the growth rate "doubles," with domestic sales robust and growing QoQ. FY26 saw structural margins up >300bps, a premiumization push (Guard 3in1, Trimmers, Oral-B Power/Sensitive), and Venus/female grooming +20%. No explicit forward revenue/margin guidance ("I cannot comment on the future").

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** No explicit company-level guidance given (repeatedly deflected; won't share price-sensitive/forward numbers). Framing: "double down" on the Integrated Growth Strategy; ambition to **grow ahead of category** while expanding it.
- **Category growth read-outs (mgmt's own):** Male Grooming category ~**12%**; Trimmers/appliances category expected **early double-digit**; ambition to grow faster than category in both.
- **Margin:** FY26 structural margins improved **>300bps**; running a **multi-year savings master plan** per business unit; explicitly **would not guide FY27 margins** ("I cannot comment on the future"), but signalled continued productivity + premium mix as levers.
- **Macro backdrop cited:** India GDP ~**6.5%** estimated for the year (slowdown vs prior-3-yr, within 10-yr trend); non-food inflation below RBI's 4% medium-term target; rural still > urban consumption but **softening** on inflation uptick; watching West Asia crisis commodity impact.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:** none disclosed (see §8).
order book & pipeline:
- Not an order-book business (FMCG). "One of the most robust innovation pipelines in recent times" — number and meaningfulness of innovations. "Exciting new lineups in the works" (undisclosed).
- Recent launches (all ~2 months before the call): **Gillette Guard 3in1**, **Gillette Trimmers (A-I-O-9 franchise)**, **Oral-B Sensitive Care** toothbrushes, Oral-B Kids packaging upgrade.
- Guard 3in1 early reads: **20cr viewers** in month 1; **~1 million razors** sold in launch month; reached **6 lakh stores**; ranked **#12 on Amazon**, tagged "Amazon's Choice" and "Bestseller" on Swiggy; brand face **Abhishek Sharma** (cricketer); campaign "Ek Stroke Mein Smooth Shave. Bina Kate, Bina Jale."
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Grooming** — every segment grew this year. **Gillette Guard** double-digit (added **20 million new users** over last 3 years); **Premium Razor** segment (Mach3/Fusion) grew **early teens**; **Female grooming / Venus** grew **upwards of 20%** and now contributes **double-digit** to the grooming business. New **Gillette Trimmers** range (four propositions) launched for beard + body grooming. Shave preps (foams/gels/after-shaves) round out the portfolio.
- **Oral Care** — **Manual** oral care growing **high single-digit**, led by newest **Oral-B Sensitive** (fastest-growing, double-digit). **Power/electric** oral care growing **~1.5x this year**; **doubled the Power Oral-B business over 3 years**; 4 new Power products launched over last 2 years. Kids line-up packaging refreshed.
- **Manufacturing/exports** — ~**85% of products manufactured domestically**; exports finished goods to **>10 countries**; actively seeking more export opportunities.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Premiumization / trade-up** — deliberate ladder across price tiers (Guard → Guard 3in1 → Mach3 → Fusion); premium razor + Power Oral-B + Trimmers are the margin-accretive up-trades.
- **Appliances (Trimmers)** — new A-I-O-9 franchise into an early-double-digit-growth category; ambition to grow faster than category and drive category growth.
- **Female grooming (Venus)** — biggest opportunity is **new-user growth**; competes vs creams / in-home wax / salons, not just other razors; scaling influencer activations + media reach.
- **Digital / GTM** — "data + human intelligence + technology"; internal models for store-level assortment; **Supply 3.0** supply-chain optimization; **advance ordering used across half the business**; **>2 million on-shelf availability data checks/day**; "double-digit portfolio optimization" already driven.
- **Channel** — winning across kirana, supermarket, e-commerce and **quick commerce**; SKUs tagged bestsellers across platforms; retailers becoming media platforms and vice-versa.
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 structural margins **+>300bps**; two levers: (1) topline premium-mix trade-up; (2) cost savings across the P&L (productivity is "more than cost-cutting," embedded in operating model, includes local-vs-import supply-chain mix).
- **Input-cost pressure (West Asia conflict):** **crude +~50%**, and consequently **resins +~50%**, with availability significantly challenged. Despite this, **no stock-outs and no product-performance compromise** — credited to business-continuity planning and supplier partnerships.
- Mitigation: always-on savings programs, securing supplies, freight-overcharge management; "balanced approach" to growth (won't sacrifice margin structure).
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- No specific capex figures, capacity numbers, or commissioning dates disclosed on the call.
- **Bhiwadi plant:** a "momentary concern" (disclosed to exchanges) was **fully resolved in a matter of days**, with **zero supply-related challenges** — supply-chain planning absorbed it.
capital allocation: - Track record of **>30 years of consistent dividend payout**; ROE doubled over 5 years while becoming more asset-efficient. Productivity ("fuel") funds superiority investment + margin expansion. No buyback / M&A / specific allocation actions disclosed.
risks & watch-items:
- **Base/optics risk:** Bangladesh affiliate distribution closure keeps reported topline growth optically muted into the coming quarters — watch when it laps out.
- **Input-cost / geopolitics:** crude & resin +50%, West Asia crisis, freight overcharges, currency headwinds — margin-structure risk if productivity can't offset.
- **Consumer softening:** rural consumption softening on inflation; discerning, value-conscious consumer; GDP decelerating to ~6.5%.
- **Competition:** management fielded multiple analyst questions on **rising competition in men's shaving** and on **muted / volatile revenue growth** — a clear investor concern despite market leadership.
- **Media fragmentation & channel shift** (agentic AI, quick commerce) raising cost/complexity of reaching consumers.
- **No forward guidance:** management declines to guide revenue or FY27 margins — limits visibility.
management quality / tone:
- Structured, strategy-heavy MD presentation (five-part "Integrated Growth Strategy": daily-use portfolio; superiority across product/pack/comms/retail/value; productivity; constructive disruption; organization). CFO handled a large pre-submitted analyst Q&A set candidly but guarded on anything price-sensitive.
- Directly addressed the two pointed investor concerns — "growth is missing"/"muted QoQ" and "rising competition" — with the Bangladesh-base explanation and category-leadership data (offtake +8%/+12%, 20m new Guard users). Credible, consistent messaging; low on hard numbers/guidance by policy.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The "muted growth" narrative is **largely a base artifact** (Bangladesh export agreement closure); management asserts domestic growth doubles ex-that and is compounding QoQ — the key thing to verify as the base laps.
- **Premium mix, not price hikes, is the margin engine** — >300bps structural gain came from consumers trading up (Guard 3in1, Power Oral-B, premium razors, Trimmers) plus P&L productivity, not commodity relief (commodities went the wrong way, +50%).
- **Power Oral-B is a quiet compounder** — doubled in 3 years, ~1.5x this year — reframing Gillette from a pure shaving name toward a broader grooming + oral-care platform.
- Supply-chain data infrastructure (>2m daily availability checks, advance ordering on half the business) is being positioned as a durable execution edge in a fragmenting quick-commerce retail landscape.

- **Oral Care** — **Manual** oral care growing **high single-digit**, led by newest **Oral-B Sensitive** (fastest-growing, double-digit). **Power/electric** oral care growing **~1.5x this year**; **doubled the Power Oral-B business over 3 years**; 4 new Power products launched over last 2 years. Kids line-up packaging refreshed.
- **Manufacturing/exports** — ~**85% of products manufactured domestically**; exports finished goods to **>10 countries**; actively seeking more export opportunities.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Premiumization / trade-up** — deliberate ladder across price tiers (Guard → Guard 3in1 → Mach3 → Fusion); premium razor + Power Oral-B + Trimmers are the margin-accretive up-trades.
- **Appliances (Trimmers)** — new A-I-O-9 franchise into an early-double-digit-growth category; ambition to grow faster than category and drive category growth.
- **Female grooming (Venus)** — biggest opportunity is **new-user growth**; competes vs creams / in-home wax / salons, not just other razors; scaling influencer activations + media reach.
- **Digital / GTM** — "data + human intelligence + technology"; internal models for store-level assortment; **Supply 3.0** supply-chain optimization; **advance ordering used across half the business**; **>2 million on-shelf availability data checks/day**; "double-digit portfolio optimization" already driven.
- **Channel** — winning across kirana, supermarket, e-commerce and **quick commerce**; SKUs tagged bestsellers across platforms; retailers becoming media platforms and vice-versa.
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 structural margins **+>300bps**; two levers: (1) topline premium-mix trade-up; (2) cost savings across the P&L (productivity is "more than cost-cutting," embedded in operating model, includes local-vs-import supply-chain mix).
- **Input-cost pressure (West Asia conflict):** **crude +~50%**, and consequently **resins +~50%**, with availability significantly challenged. Despite this, **no stock-outs and no product-performance compromise** — credited to business-continuity planning and supplier partnerships.
- Mitigation: always-on savings programs, securing supplies, freight-overcharge management; "balanced approach" to growth (won't sacrifice margin structure).
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- No specific capex figures, capacity numbers, or commissioning dates disclosed on the call.
- **Bhiwadi plant:** a "momentary concern" (disclosed to exchanges) was **fully resolved in a matter of days**, with **zero supply-related challenges** — supply-chain planning absorbed it.
capital allocation: - Track record of **>30 years of consistent dividend payout**; ROE doubled over 5 years while becoming more asset-efficient. Productivity ("fuel") funds superiority investment + margin expansion. No buyback / M&A / specific allocation actions disclosed.
risks & watch-items:
- **Base/optics risk:** Bangladesh affiliate distribution closure keeps reported topline growth optically muted into the coming quarters — watch when it laps out.
- **Input-cost / geopolitics:** crude & resin +50%, West Asia crisis, freight overcharges, currency headwinds — margin-structure risk if productivity can't offset.
- **Consumer softening:** rural consumption softening on inflation; discerning, value-conscious consumer; GDP decelerating to ~6.5%.
- **Competition:** management fielded multiple analyst questions on **rising competition in men's shaving** and on **muted / volatile revenue growth** — a clear investor concern despite market leadership.
- **Media fragmentation & channel shift** (agentic AI, quick commerce) raising cost/complexity of reaching consumers.
- **No forward guidance:** management declines to guide revenue or FY27 margins — limits visibility.
management quality / tone:
- Structured, strategy-heavy MD presentation (five-part "Integrated Growth Strategy": daily-use portfolio; superiority across product/pack/comms/retail/value; productivity; constructive disruption; organization). CFO handled a large pre-submitted analyst Q&A set candidly but guarded on anything price-sensitive.
- Directly addressed the two pointed investor concerns — "growth is missing"/"muted QoQ" and "rising competition" — with the Bangladesh-base explanation and category-leadership data (offtake +8%/+12%, 20m new Guard users). Credible, consistent messaging; low on hard numbers/guidance by policy.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The "muted growth" narrative is **largely a base artifact** (Bangladesh export agreement closure); management asserts domestic growth doubles ex-that and is compounding QoQ — the key thing to verify as the base laps.
- **Premium mix, not price hikes, is the margin engine** — >300bps structural gain came from consumers trading up (Guard 3in1, Power Oral-B, premium razors, Trimmers) plus P&L productivity, not commodity relief (commodities went the wrong way, +50%).
- **Power Oral-B is a quiet compounder** — doubled in 3 years, ~1.5x this year — reframing Gillette from a pure shaving name toward a broader grooming + oral-care platform.
- Supply-chain data infrastructure (>2m daily availability checks, advance ordering on half the business) is being positioned as a durable execution edge in a fragmenting quick-commerce retail landscape.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company, incorporated in India in 1984 as Indian Shaving Products Limited and acquired by P&G in 2005, is engaged in manufacturing and selling branded packaged fast moving consumer goods in the grooming and oral care businesses. Its portfolio spans blades, razors and toiletries under the Gillette family of brands and oral care under Oral-B, serving Indian consumers across traditional shaving, hassle-free and advanced grooming needs as well as female grooming. Management describes it as one of the well-known FMCG companies, with a reputation for delivering superior products through superior value propositions to Indian consumers.

demand_drivers.body:
- India is expected to remain the world's fastest growing major economy, with growth projected at 6.4% in 2026-27, driven by strong domestic demand
- IMF July 2026 World Economic Outlook projects global growth at 3% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, described as a V-shaped recovery balancing geo-political conflict shocks against artificial intelligence tech booms
- Global headline inflation projected to rise to 4.7% in 2026 from 4.1% in 2025 before declining to 3.9% in 2027
- Evolving global trade policies and commodity prices need to be watched as they will impact inflation and cost of goods produced
- Indian FMCG: non-food inflation continues to stay below RBI's medium-term target of 4%, while consumer consumption trends are still shifting
- Rural consumption continues to be higher than urban consumption but is showing a softening trend driven by an uptick in inflation rates
- FMCG sector expected to enter a stabilization phase and a period of renewed optimism, with projections focused on volume-led growth rather than price-driven expansion
- Urban demand continues to anchor growth, aided by premiumisation across categories

capex_expansion.body: The routed sections disclose no named plant, capacity or capex project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Expansion in this Annual Report is described in market-reach rather than asset terms: the Company continued to expand the reach of Gillette Guard through focused communication and strong market execution, launched Gillette Guard 3-in-1, strengthened the Mach3 range, and in Oral Care pursued a strategic focus on expanding penetration of electric toothbrushes, launched kids' battery toothbrushes and its biggest-ever launch in the sensitive toothbrush category, working to make the Sensitive Care range widely available across channels and segments through e-commerce and general trade activations.
